Evaluations for each agent stage plus the closed feedback loops that keep the production system aligned.
sources: transcript context (intro; 'generation of the vowels' before 'pairwise comparison')

terms.definition: The production system under discussion: edits food photography to better present dishes for smaller, independent Uber Eats merchants while staying faithful to the dish, preserving merchant brand/packaging, and avoiding marketplace homogenization.

First pipeline stage: a multimodal LLM describes the photo, the description becomes structured output, and a router applies pass/fail rubric criteria to decide enhance vs skip (skip keeps the original). Evaled as a classifier with a confusion matrix (2x2, or n x n when routing to multiple branches/models).
Second pipeline stage; runs in a feedback loop with the QA agent, self-correcting edits; after a number of failed loops the image is not published.

Multi-dimensional quality gate over plating, faithfulness, colors, etc.; failed edits loop back with feedback. The final 'post-processing and publish-ready QA' adds policy checks and redundancy (Swiss cheese model).
The router's evaluation frame: true positives, false negatives, and related outcomes used to measure precision and recall; it generalizes to an n x n matrix for multi-branch routing.
Classifier metrics used to evaluate routing; recall is the key guardrail because unsafe images must not slip through.

Human-labeled representative dataset (cuts across geographies, dish types, image quality) treated as the golden source of truth; agents are tuned until they meet guardrail metrics against it, and re-benchmarked against it after every auto-tune.
Ship/no-ship thresholds the tuned agent must meet on the golden dataset (recall for routing); part of the 'ship safely' theme.
Failure mode example: a dish named 'eight pieces chicken wings' whose photo shows six; an enhancement model may hallucinate the two missing wings to match the description — a faithfulness failure.
The higher-level abstraction over all feedback loops: it takes flagged input, identifies which agents need optimization, localizes the issue, and triggers the auto-tuning pipeline.

Config-driven, no-human-in-the-loop tuning triggered by the diagnoser: tunes the target agent, benchmarks against the golden dataset, ships on pass, iterates otherwise; runs on a regular cadence over sampled production data, with observability guardrails and quick rollback.
The auto-tuning core: given unseen human-labeled eval samples it finds mismatches and rewrites the target agent's config. Composed of two sub-agents, reflect and synthesize.
Prompt-optimizer sub-agent that inspects mismatches, removes noise, finds systemic issues in the dataset, and sends feedback to the synthesize agent.
Prompt-optimizer sub-agent that combines the reflect agent's feedback with the current agent configuration, writes a new configuration, and benchmarks it.
Registry where a newly benchmark-passing agent version is registered so production can pick it up on the next run.

Enhancement-loop metric: pass rate at the Kth iteration; rises with iterations as feedback accumulates. Enhancement ends in publish (QA pass within K iterations) or a coverage hit (image never enhanced).
sources: transcript context (enhancement section: 'pass at K' / 'Kth iteration')

terms.definition: How 'better' is judged for pass@K: the input and output images are compared directly, output graded yes/no/unsure against the platform's baked-in definition of a better image (faithful, complete, natural, realistic, …), aligned with product, design, policy, and legal.

Failure mode where the editing agent oversteers after a QA rejection into an overly conservative, nugatory change (falling back to a generic ceramic bowl) whose raw pixels differ but which is not a meaningful or influential change.
A change that is not meaningful or influential despite differing pixels; the talk's term for the reward-hacked edit.
Core eval dimension: the edit must not add or invent content (example failure: shrimp added to the dish). Pair with completeness.
sources: video description ('stay faithful to the original dish')

terms.definition: Eval dimension complementary to faithfulness: the edit must not remove content (example failure: sauce at the bottom of the sushi removed).

Eval dimensions where frontier image-editing models' problems leak into the applied use case (example: the plate covering the sauce in the output); Uber's evals sometimes surface these back to the frontier teams.
Defense-in-depth rationale for the redundant publish-ready QA gate: stacked imperfect layers reduce the chance of a failure reaching production.

The first and predominant feedback loop: accounts for drift by aligning to the offline human-labeled dataset (sample production data at cadence → label → mismatch → diagnoser → auto-tune → benchmark → ship).
Uber's internal feedback culture: teams test apps before launch, then replay production ratings and free-form feedback from merchants, design, and product teams into the diagnoser.
The called-out marketplace metric: add-to-cart, converting, completing orders; production impact is sliced by geos, device type, dish type, etc., and segments can be tuned individually.
The router input format: the multimodal LLM's image description is converted to a structured form that is graded against a pass/fail rubric.
Enhancement-loop terminal outcome where the image is never enhanced after K failed iterations; traded off against publishing bad edits.
